slides.texte_overlay:
How to stay calm in social
situations that scare you
Name what you're feeling. "I'm nervous, and that's okay." Saying it to yourself takes away half its power and helps you stay steady.
Focus on one person at a time. Big groups feel overwhelming. Talking to one person is much easier, and others often join in.
Use your senses to ground yourself. Notice three things you can see, two you can hear, one you can touch. It brings you back to the moment.
Prepare a way out. Knowing you can leave after an hour makes it easier to go. Most of the time, you'll want to stay longer.
Before: I panicked when conversations went quiet. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and I always have something to say.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: I panicked when conversations went quiet. After: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. I always have something to say.

slides.texte_overlay: Practise in easy places first. A café, a shop, a gym class. Small, low-pressure chats build confidence for bigger situations.
Be proud of every step. Going, staying, talking to one new person. Progress with anxiety is made of small wins, and each one counts.
